sourceFile: "Diocesan-Cycle-of-Prayer-2026-May-Dec-updated-4-22-2026.docx", provided directly by Josh via Google Drive (file id 1pzQxvQKN0H-MF4KaXtgtvMYDdret594o, folder "TEC Cycle of Prayer").
notes: This source only covers May 3 through December 27, 2026 (35 weeks) -- it is itself titled 'May-Dec-updated' and its own text begins at May. This is the source's own real scope, not a gap trimmed by this transcription; no January-April 2026 weeks exist to ingest.

Each week prints three or four lines beyond the parish name(s): a 'The ministries of [clergy list]' line (a rotating roll of clergy, not tied to the week's own named parish) and a 'The work of [committee/ministry]' line, both recorded as their own `category` subjects, per this corpus's established pattern for a diocese-wide standing-intercession line that isn't itself a parish. Several weeks substitute a 'The churches in the [Saint] Regional Ministry Network' category (with a 'Patron saint commemorated on [date]' `note`) or an 'In thanksgiving for the ministry of the Rt. Rev. [name]' / 'The ministry of the Rt. Rev. [name]' category (with a 'Consecrated/Became/Installed Nth Bishop...' `note`) in place of the 'work of' line -- both are the source's own substitution, not this transcription's choice.

'The Community of St. John Baptist, Mendham' (June 7) is an Episcopal religious order (an Anglican convent), not a parish -- recorded as a `category` subject with the place folded into its own name, matching this corpus's existing precedent for a religious community (see episcopal-great-lakes-2026.json's Emmaus Monastery/St. Gregory's Abbey entries) rather than as a `parish` subject.

November 8 is the only week with three category subjects instead of two: alongside the usual clergy-ministries line, the source prints both a bishop-thanksgiving line ('In thanksgiving for the ministry of the Rt. Rev. William H. Odenheimer... upon the founding of this diocese') AND a separate 'The work of the Annual Diocesan Convention' line noting its own dates ('Friday & Saturday, November 13 & 14') -- both preserved as distinct subjects rather than merged.

All punctuation (en dashes, curly apostrophes, ampersands within a single parish's own name such as 'St. Paul's & Resurrection' or 'Epiphany & Christ Church') is transcribed exactly as the source prints it.
